subject.title: System prompt should prefer Skill tool over read when available

question: Should OpenClaw support a plugin-provided Skill loader in the native Skills prompt by raw tool name, by an explicit trusted capability or manifest contract, or defer this until broader skill-contract parity work is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but deciding how plugin tool output becomes higher-authority skill-loading context changes the plugin trust boundary and prompt contract, which automation should not settle.

options.title: Require Explicit Skill-Loader Contract
options.body: Add a named trusted capability or manifest/SDK contract before changing prompt wording, so only intentionally declared loader tools receive the stronger loading instruction.

options.title: Use Normalized Tool Name Detection
options.body: Treat any available tool named Skill as the loader and update the prompt now, accepting collision and trust-boundary risk for a smaller change.

options.title: Defer To Broader Skill Contract Work
options.body: Keep the read-based prompt until native/Codex parity and slash-invocation skill-loading semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Require Explicit Skill-Loader Contract
recommendation.body: Add a named trusted capability or manifest/SDK contract before changing prompt wording, so only intentionally declared loader tools receive the stronger loading instruction.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history on the system prompt surface and adjacent prompt/plugin-boundary changes.
